canonical_question: Did Senkov et al.'s 2011 work [19] on WMoTaNbV establish the baseline mechanical properties for this specific alloy system?

question_variants.question: Did Senkov et al.'s 2011 work [19] on WMoTaNbV establish the baseline mechanical properties for this specific alloy system?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The provided evidence mentions that results on WMoTaNbV were reported by Senkov et al. in 2011, but does not contain the specific mechanical property data or confirm if it established a 'baseline' for this specific system compared to other metrics.

answers.answer: The text confirms that results on WMoTaNbV were reported by Senkov et al. in 2011, but does not provide the specific mechanical values or context to determine if this established a baseline for the specific alloy system in the current work.
answers.boundary_limitation: No specific property values or baseline context provided in text.
evidence_spans: A PBF-LB/M machine of the type AconityMINI (Aconity GmbH, Herzogenrath, Germany) was used for manufacturing cubic samples with an edge length of 6 mm on molybdenum substrate plates obtained from Plansee SE (Reutte, Austria).
The machine is equipped with a redPower QUBE single mode fiber laser from SPI Lasers Ltd. (Southamton, UK) featuring an operating wavelength of 1080 nm and a maximum power of 1 kW.
The scanner optics used is an AxialScan-30 from Raylase GmbH (Wessling, Germany).

source_evidence_spans: First results on the alloys WMoTaNb and WMoTaNbV were reported by Senkov et al., in 2010 [ [18] ] and 2011 [ [19] ], respectively.
